title: Geo-aware staggered safety drain with SLO-bridging and operator playbook
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Problem: Our current regional cutover and blue/green flows can cause simultaneous capacity pressure across adjacent regions during large-scale hosted API upgrades. This manifests as transient p90/p99 spikes, cache miss amplification, and occasional autoscaler thrash when traffic is shifted too quickly.

Goal: Implement a geo-aware staggered drain mechanism that shifts traffic between regions with a configurable stagger window, built-in SLO-bridging (temporary, bounded relaxation of non-critical SLOs), and automated rollback triggers. Provide an operator playbook and automated tests so on-call can run predictable regional rollouts with minimal customer impact.

Scope: Hosted API pipeline only (control-plane and data-plane traffic routing). Not in scope: Dedicated private deployments (separate ticket).

Design overview:
- Staggered drain controller: orchestrates per-region drain windows. Default stagger: 10m (configurable via rollout policy). The controller will: request gradual weight decay from source region, wait drain-window, validate canary signals, then continue.
- SLO-bridging: for the duration of a regional drain window, non-critical latency SLOs (p95) are temporarily relaxed by a bounded factor and recorded as bridged events in the audit log. Critical error rate SLOs remain hard gates.
- Gate checks: each step requires pass/fail evaluation of a small set of metrics (p50 latency delta, p95 latency delta, 5xx rate, cold-start count, queue length). Failure during a window triggers automated rollback per configured policy.
- Circuit integration: tie into existing circuit-breaker service so downstream services can opt-in to graceful degradation signals emitted during a drain.
- Observability: new Grafana dashboards and templated alert rules (rollout-bridge, bridge-duration-exceeded, rollback-triggered) plus a single pane rollout timeline.
- Operator runbook: step-by-step playbook with manual escalation, CLI commands for forced rollback, and post-mortem checklist.

Acceptance criteria:
- New controller can perform a full multi-region swap on staging without violating hard error-rate gates.
- SLO-bridging events are visible in audit logs and associated with rollout ID.
- Automated rollback fires when p95 delta > 40% for three consecutive windows or 5xx rate increases > 0.5%.
- Graphs and alerts deliver actionable signal with < 2m alerting latency.
- E2E tests simulate surge traffic and verify stagger windows prevent autoscaler thrash.

Implementation plan (high level):
1) Prototype controller and stagger policy in canary environment (eu-west-1) — Liam (owner).
2) Implement SLO-bridging feature flag and audit logging — Maya + infra-security review.
3) Add gate evaluation library and define default thresholds in rollout-policy repo.
4) Build observability dashboards and alerting runbook templates — Metrics team.
5) Author operator playbook and CLI extension for forced rollback.
6) Run cross-region chaos tests and finalize thresholds.

Test plan:
- Load tests with synthetic traffic to validate p95/p99 behavior under staggered shifts.
- Chaos tests that kill a region during a drain to validate rollback safety.
- Integration tests for rollout timeline and audit linkage.

Rollout and timeline:
- Week 1 (prototype): canary validation in eu-west-1.
- Week 2 (iteration): integrate SLO-bridging and gate library, security review.
- Week 3 (staging): full multi-region simulation.
- Week 4 (prod): gated rollout behind feature flag and manual operator approval.

Notes on safety and trade-offs:
- Bridging latency SLO temporarily accepts higher latency to avoid cascading failures; must be limited in duration and tracked to prevent abuse.
- Conservative defaults will bias safety over speed; teams can opt into more aggressive stagger windows for low-latency non-critical workloads.
